hook.text: Twice a day, the ocean rises and falls—pulled by the gravity of the Moon and Sun.

buildup.text: The Moon's gravity pulls water on the near side of Earth toward it, creating a tidal bulge.

discovery.text: A second bulge forms on the far side because Earth is pulled away from that water.

twist.text: When the Sun and Moon align (spring tides), tidal range is extreme; at right angles (neap tides), it's mild.

climax.text: Canada's Bay of Fundy sees 16-meter tides—the highest on Earth, driven by its funnel shape.

punchline.text: The Moon lifts the entire ocean—twice every day.

quiz.question: What causes tides?
options: Gravitational pull of the Moon and Sun
